question: Who became the new CEO of Dow in July 2026?

## Karen S\. Carter Appointed as CEO; Board Expands to Include New Director Dow Inc\. DOW has announced a significant leadership transition, appointing Karen S\. Carter as the new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1, 2026\. This appointment follows the decision of the current CEO, Jim Fitterling, to transition to the role of Executive Chair of the Board\. Mr\. Fitterling will continue to serve as a Director until the 2027 Annual Meeting of Stockholders or until a successor is duly elected and qualified\. Ms\. Carter, who has been with Dow for over three decades, brings extensive experience to her new role\. She has been serving as Dow's Chief Operating Officer since December 2024, overseeing business and operational performance across the company\. Her previous roles include President of Dow's Packaging & Specialty Plastics business segment and Chief Human Resources Officer and Chief Inclusion Officer\. In addition to her appointment as CEO, Ms\. Carter will also join the Board of Directors, expanding the Board from twelve to thirteen members\. # Dow's new CEO is blessed to be stressed \| Fortune Karen S\. Carter is blessed to be stressed\. She’s the new CEO of Dow, 30 years into her career at the chemicals business\. Her accolades include: one of three Black female CEOs in the Fortune 500, the first woman and first Black person to run almost 130-year-old Dow, and No\. 88 on the 2026 Most Powerful Women list\. Carter officially started her role on July 1 and presided over her first earnings report as CEO last week\. Meanwhile, the company is grappling with financial losses, a corporate restructuring, thousands of layoffs, and the shuttering of some European plants\. But this is what the CEO recently told my colleague Jordan Blum, *Fortune*‘s energy editor\. “There’s a saying that it’s a blessing to be stressed by the thing you prayed for and hoped for,” she said\. “This is really a privilege and an honor to be leading this company in such a time of change\.” Anyone in Carter’s position would be stressed, really\.
